about_en: Maximilian Reinke develops tools and applications with a focus on privacy, system-level functionality, and user-centric workflows. His projects include a browser-based image processing tool for anonymizing license plates, a Linux-specific fork of GitHub Desktop tailored for a custom distribution, and utilities for input remapping, secure environment variable management, and bias lighting for Linux systems. These projects often emphasize local processing, platform-specific optimizations, and seamless integration with existing workflows.

In his technical approach, Maximilian employs a diverse set of programming languages and tools, including Rust, Python, TypeScript, and WGSL. His work frequently involves low-level system programming, GPU-accelerated computations, and terminal-based user interfaces. He leverages technologies such as evdev, uinput, systemd, and wgpu to build efficient and maintainable solutions. Dockerfiles and shell scripting are also part of his toolkit for managing development environments and deployment processes.
about_de: Maximilian Reinke entwickelt Tools und Anwendungen mit einem Schwerpunkt auf Datenschutz, systemnaher Funktionalität und benutzerzentrierten Workflows. Zu seinen Projekten gehören ein browserbasiertes Bildbearbeitungstool zur Anonymisierung von Kennzeichen, ein Linux-spezifischer Fork von GitHub Desktop für eine angepasste Distribution sowie Werkzeuge zur Eingabeneuverknüpfung, sicheren Verwaltung von Umgebungsvariablen und Bias-Beleuchtung für Linux-Systeme. Diese Projekte legen oft Wert auf lokale Verarbeitung, plattformspezifische Optimierungen und nahtlose Integration in bestehende Workflows.

In seiner technischen Herangehensweise verwendet Maximilian eine Vielzahl von Programmiersprachen und Werkzeugen, darunter Rust, Python, TypeScript und WGSL. Seine Arbeit umfasst häufig systemnahe Programmierung, GPU-beschleunigte Berechnungen und terminalbasierte Benutzeroberflächen. Er nutzt Technologien wie evdev, uinput, systemd und wgpu, um effiziente und wartbare Lösungen zu entwickeln. Dockerfiles und Shell-Skripte gehören ebenfalls zu seinem Werkzeugkasten für die Verwaltung von Entwicklungsumgebungen und Bereitstellungsprozessen.
about_en_casual: xi72yow is into building practical tools and fun side projects, mostly for Linux and the web. They’ve got a mix of stuff going on, from a browser-based app for editing license plates in photos to a zombie survival game you can play with a friend on one keyboard. A lot of their work leans toward solving niche problems, like remapping input devices at the kernel level or syncing screen colors with WLED lights. They also seem to care about security and usability, with projects like a tool for managing environment variables securely using GNOME Keyring.

When it comes to tech, xi72yow keeps things pretty diverse. They write in Rust, Python, TypeScript, and even WGSL for GPU stuff. Their repos show a knack for working with Linux-specific tools like systemd and Wayland, and they’re comfortable with Docker for containerized workflows. They seem to prefer clean, efficient solutions, whether it’s using a terminal UI for configuration or integrating directly with the system. Overall, their projects feel like a mix of curiosity and practicality, with a solid focus on making things work well in their chosen environments.

last_commits.message:
feat: node drive backup/restore and model download as a build arg

Replaces the rclone sync with versioned snapshots, which also gives history: a
mirror would happily sync a corrupted dataset over the only copy.

- tools/backup.mjs: zip the given paths straight into the upload (no temp file),
  keep the newest N snapshots, drop the rest
- tools/restore.mjs: list/download/unpack; defaults to a fresh restore-<stamp>/
  dir, only --into overwrites in place. The archive keeps the relative layout so
  --into . puts everything back where it came from
- tools/drive.mjs: shared auth. Plain user OAuth (browser once), refresh token in
  the OS keyring, never on disk. Scope drive.file, so the tool can only ever see
  files it created itself
- --latest replaces the content of the SAME drive file every run, so the model's
  id and download url stay stable across retrains; prune is restricted to the
  snapshot zips so it can never eat that artifact
- Containerfile: MODEL_URL build arg fetches the pose model into public/ before
  the vite build (Coolify build argument). The model is gitignored, so images
  built so far shipped without it. Builds fine without the arg, the app then just
  has no auto-suggest
- rclone kept as backup:rclone / restore:rclone so the existing drive data stays
  reachable

Auth gotcha worth remembering: @google-cloud/local-auth pulls google-auth-library
^9 while googleapis pulls ^10, so npm keeps two copies and a client from local-auth
fails googleapis' instanceof check, which silently sends unauthenticated requests.
local-auth is therefore only used to obtain the refresh token.
last_commits.author: xi72yow

last_commits.message:
feat: dedup gate, roboflow harvest, and labelling-harness fixes

- dedup.py (npm run dedup): perceptual near-dup gate, dHash + MobileNet cosine;
  dHash clusters pin a leak-free train/val split via dataset/clusters.json, CNN
  pairs are advisory-only in a review montage (cosine cannot separate a true
  near-dup from same-category by threshold)
- dataset.py: cluster-aware split (splits on the cluster representative, falls
  back to the stem when clusters.json is absent)
- harvest.py (npm run harvest): filter the roboflow YOLOv8 export by filename
  family into inbox/, dHash cross-dedup vs the dataset and internally
- fix: ?annotate hung ~20s/image because #autodetect stayed disabled under the
  "soon" rollout phase, so waitDetect() polled to its timeout; detectOn() enables
  detection in annotate mode independent of phaseOn
- annotate: HUD timing log (model load / inference / decode) + terminal per-step
  logging; instant save/skip feedback while the next image loads
- train_scratch.py: RUN SUMMARY prints the POSE_CONF operating-point sweep
- detect.js/main.js: POSE_CONF 0.5 shipped operating point + live confidence
  slider; detection timing hooks
- docs: MODEL-PLAN dedup gate, README inbox portal
